_metadata.independence: Apart from the brief, I read only x18-rb-input.json; I opened no other repository file, ran no search and used no web or paid API.

hints.reason: AMAZON via the Amazon river dolphin and PINK via its famous pink colour; the pink river dolphin is a well-known nature fact and the link clicks nicely.

pairs.pair_note: Good fact-based pair; the pink boto is familiar from nature documentaries and kids' animal books.

hints.reason: BABY via the folklore of the stork delivering babies and BIRD because a stork is a bird; easy but clean and universally known.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, obvious and satisfying; a place-plus-category style link like PENGUIN.

hints.reason: BOTTLE via a cork stopper and BARK via cork being the bark of the cork oak; the bark side is a nice indirect aha that most players know or accept instantly.

pairs.pair_note: Strong indirect-knowledge hint; facts are accurate.

hints.reason: DOG via Mickey's dog Pluto and BELT via the dwarf planet Pluto in the Kuiper Belt; the BELT side needs school-level astronomy but the dog/planet double meaning gives a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Kuiper Belt is the weaker half; many players will recall it from the Pluto demotion news, but some may hunt for Orion's Belt or asteroid belt first. Worth a second opinion on familiarity.

hints.reason: Both sides through Goldfinger: BOND via the classic 1964 James Bond film and FINGER because the title is GOLD + FINGER (gold rings on fingers is a secondary route); Gold Bond powder is a bonus echo.

pairs.pair_note: The FINGER line leans on gold rings, which is the weaker route; the real click is the title Goldfinger itself. Accurate as written.

hints.reason: BOTTLE via the instantly familiar phrase message in a bottle, and NOTE because the message in such a bottle is a note; the synonym side is honest and the pairing is a pleasant picture.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but fair; the phrase is iconic.

hints.reason: BRUSH via grooming (brushing a horse, pet or hair) and WEDDING via the groom; a clean, DRIVER-style double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent double meaning.

hints.reason: Both sides via the nursery rhyme Jack Be Nimble (Jack jumps over the candlestick), with jumping jacks as a bonus JUMP echo; a well-known rhyme that clicks immediately.
hints.fix: CANDLE line: "A candlestick is a holder for a candle, and Jack jumps over one in the rhyme."

pairs.pair_note: The CANDLE line implies the rhyme mentions a candle on the stick; the suggested line keeps it to what the rhyme says.

hints.reason: CARPET via Persian rugs and CAT via the Persian breed; two very familiar uses of one word.

pairs.pair_note: Classic, fair and satisfying.

hints.reason: CAST via actors learning lines (and casting a line) and FISHING via fishing line; a neat double meaning with a bonus overlap.

pairs.pair_note: Solid double meaning; LINE is generic on a big board but fair.

hints.reason: CHANGE via the werewolf's transformation and MOON via the full moon that triggers it in legend and film; universally known.

pairs.pair_note: Clear and fair; the text keeps it to legend and stories.

hints.reason: CHICK via a hen raising her chicks and MOTHER via the phrase mother hen; easy and pleasant.
hints.fix: Explanation: "A hen is a female chicken that can hatch and raise chicks, and a fussy, protective person is called a mother hen."

pairs.pair_note: The explanation defines a hen as a mother chicken; a hen is any adult female chicken, so the fix softens it.

hints.reason: CLOUD and GROUND together via the familiar fact that fog is a cloud at ground level; a tidy aha once seen.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate and satisfying.

hints.reason: COFFEE via joe as slang for coffee and CUP via the instantly familiar phrase cup of joe; a fun, easy slang clue.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but cup of joe is instantly familiar to U.S. players and more fun than MUG.

hints.reason: Both sides via Aesop's The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse; COUNTRY mouse is also an everyday phrase, and TOWN works even though many Americans know the city mouse version.

pairs.pair_note: Familiar fable; lines are accurate summaries.

hints.reason: DICE via Yahtzee's five dice and CUP via the shaker cup that comes with the game; a vivid, family-game-night picture.

pairs.pair_note: Brand hint that most U.S. players know well; both sides honest.

hints.reason: Both sides via Punxsutawney Phil, the groundhog of Groundhog Day (and Bill Murray's Phil in the film); an indirect aha that cleanly splits the compound into GROUND and DAY.

pairs.pair_note: Clever and fair; GROUNDHOG itself would contain a target, so PHIL is the right indirect route.

hints.reason: VOLCANO via lava and DESSERT via molten lava cake; the dessert side is a delightful twist.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair.

hints.reason: DISH via the idiom dish the dirt (gossip) and MUD via mud being wet dirt; familiar idiom plus a literal link.

pairs.pair_note: PIE (pie dish, mud pie) is an equally good alternative, not clearly better.

hints.reason: RABBIT via the Energizer Bunny mascot and DRUM via the bass drum it famously beats; a vivid, well-known ad icon.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent brand-mascot hint; lines are accurate.

hints.reason: FAIRYTALE via happily ever after and END because that phrase is the classic ending (and a fairytale ending is a happy end); instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: END side is slightly softer but still clicks because the phrase literally closes the story.

hints.reason: FALL via tripping (a stumble that makes you fall) and VACATION via a trip away; a clean, everyday double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Good DRIVER-style double meaning.

hints.reason: FIREFIGHTER via fire hoses and GARDEN via the garden hose; obvious but clean and satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Easy clue; low delight is fine.

hints.reason: FLAME via the Olympic flame and TORCH via the Olympic torch relay; both are fixed, famous phrases.

pairs.pair_note: The targets are already close in meaning, so the hint mainly specifies the context; still fair and pleasant.

hints.reason: GENIUS via Einstein as a byword for genius and TONGUE via his famous 1951 tongue-out photo; an iconic image that gives a real oh-nice moment.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch; facts accurate.

hints.reason: GREECE via Homer's ancient Greek epic and TRIP via odyssey meaning a long eventful journey; a satisfying literary double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: HALLOWEEN via the jack-o'-lantern is instant, but TURNIP relies on the Irish and Scottish turnip-lantern origin, a fun fact many U.S. players would not link unprompted (close to the EXCALIBUR-lake hold).

pairs.pair_note: Facts are true and the reveal is delightful, but the TURNIP side is trivia-dependent; genuinely unsure whether the owner sees this as fun indirect knowledge or as an obscure legend detail.

hints.reason: ITALY via its boot shape and HEEL via a boot's heel (and the heel of Italy's boot); clean and satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; lines accurate.

hints.reason: SNAKE because a cobra is a snake and HOOD via the cobra's flared hood; a category-plus-property link like PENGUIN.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and familiar.

hints.reason: Both sides via Long John Silver of Treasure Island, with silver itself being treasure as a bonus; an indirect literary aha.

pairs.pair_note: Good indirect route; better than the flat PIRATE.

hints.reason: Both sides via the instantly familiar phrase the new kid on the block and the band New Kids on the Block; a phrase-join, but a very well-known one.
hints.fix: NEW line: "NEW starts both the phrase \"new kid on the block\" and the band name New Kids on the Block."

pairs.pair_note: The NEW line is awkward ("puts NEW before the block"); the fix makes it clear.

hints.reason: Both sides via the Knights of the Round Table of Arthurian legend; instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join plus legend; easy and fair.

hints.reason: LINE via hanging laundry on a clothesline and PIN via the clothespins that hold it; a clear, familiar scene.

pairs.pair_note: CLOTHES (clothesline, clothespin) is a slightly tighter alternative, but LAUNDRY is not clearly weaker; both can pass.

hints.reason: MAN via Superman's nickname the Man of Steel and STRONG via steel's strength (strong as steel); familiar on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: STRONG side is a bit generic but honest; Superman being super strong reinforces it.

hints.reason: MILK via coconut milk and PALM via the coconut palm; straightforward and accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair.

hints.reason: NEST via crows building nests and SHIP via the crow's nest lookout on a mast; a satisfying bird-to-ship twist.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: POETRY via rhyme and ORANGE via the famous fact that orange has no common perfect rhyme; a witty indirect aha.

pairs.pair_note: The explanation wisely says "no common perfect rhyme" (obscure words like sporange exist). Explanation could mention poetry too, but the line covers it.

hints.reason: POINT via point-blank and PISTOL via starter and prop pistols firing blanks; two different senses of blank that click together.

pairs.pair_note: Good; tone stays PG (starter and prop pistols).

hints.reason: Both sides via the classic image of a pupil bringing an apple for the teacher, with apple of my eye as a bonus PUPIL echo.

pairs.pair_note: Classic and fair.

hints.reason: SAND via the sand that runs through an hourglass and TIME via its role as a timer and symbol of time; obvious but satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, clean.

hints.reason: SHOT because a putt is a golf shot and SINK via the familiar phrase sink a putt; fair sports language.

pairs.pair_note: Fair; SINK is the nice non-obvious side.

hints.reason: Both sides via a snake's forked tongue (and the idiom speak with forked tongue); FORK as a kitchen word makes it a pleasant small leap.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate and fair.

hints.reason: STORM via the compound stormtrooper and STAR WARS via the Empire's stormtroopers; the compound is instantly familiar and the Star Wars link is iconic.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but a very familiar one; TROOPER also misdirects nicely toward state trooper.

hints.reason: TASTE via the compound taste bud and TONGUE because most taste buds sit on the tongue; familiar and accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair; the TONGUE line correctly says most rather than all.
